PLACING ADDITIONAL POSITIONS IN LEVELS IV AND V OF THE  
FEDERAL EXECUTIVE SALARY SCHEDULE
By virtue of the authority vested in me by subsection ( f ) of section  
303 of the Government Employees Salary Reform Act of 1964, and as  
President of the United States, Executive Order No. 11248 of October  
10,1965, as amended, is further amended as follows:

IV  of the Federal Executive Salary Schedule, is amended by adding  
thereto the following:
(4) Executive Secretary, President’s Commission on Law Enforce­
ment and Administration of Justice.
Sec. 2. Section 2 of that Order, placing certain positions in Level  
of the Federal Executive Salary Schedule, is amended by addii  
thereto the following:
(4) Director, Bureau of Outdoor Recreation, Department of the  
Interior.
(5) Assistant to the Secretary of Defense (Legislative Affairs).
Lyndon B. J ohnson
T he W hite  H ouse,
December 13 , 1965.

reported_material_gaps: Clause EO:11262#sec1-item4-level-IV: the actual termination date of the President's Commission on Law Enforcement and Administration of Justice is not in held sources (EO 11236: terminate not later than 90 days after the final report). The clause ended on that date or, at the latest, on 1968-04-29 (EO 11409 item 1(b)). Needs the commission's report and termination record.
versions.research_rationale: EO 11262 adds three items to EO 11248: in level IV, (4) Executive Secretary of the President's Commission on Law Enforcement and Administration of Justice; in level V, (4) Director, Bureau of Outdoor Recreation and (5) Assistant to the Secretary of Defense (Legislative Affairs). No later amender deleted the two level V items (traced item by item through EO 11699); they ended with EO 11708 sec. 3 on March 23, 1973. EO 11409 item 1(b) formally deleted the level IV item on April 29, 1968. That position, however, belonged to a temporary commission: EO 11236 (held, 30 FR 9349) required the commission to report within 18 months and to terminate not later than 90 days after its report. The placement therefore probably lost its object before the 1968 deletion. Deadlines cannot fix the actual date, so that clause's first_end stays open. The whole-order end is unaffected because the two level V items ran to 1973-03-23. Family method: the researcher read the saved official Federal Register OCR text layers (heading to FR Doc line) of this order, of EO 11248 and of all 40 orders that the OFR disposition notes and the 1989 Codification list as amending it, plus EO 11708, 11715, 11736 and 11768, and traced every item of EO 11248 sections 1 and 2 through each addition, deletion, word substitution and renumbering. EO 11708 sec. 3 (signed and filed March 23, 1973; no other effective date) revokes EO 11248 as amended, except for the eight positions listed in its section 2; none of them is a position whose placement this order's text still supplied. Where a later amender deletes an item and inserts another in its place, the earlier item's placement ends on that amender's effective date; the series' separate 'substituting for the words' formula is treated as a retitling that continues the item. Pure deletions, renumberings and effective-date provisions are one-time edits completed when the order took effect. The 5 U.S.C. 5315-5316 amendment notes for 1964-1973 record no statutory placement of the positions concerned. Abolition of a position by unpublished departmental action is outside the held sources and is a limitation of this bounded search. Page images were not viewed; quotations are exact from the saved OCR, including its recognition errors. No human certification is asserted.

savings_residuals.reason: The order only placed, removed or renumbered positions in pay levels IV and V of the Executive Schedule under 5 U.S.C. 5317 (formerly sec. 303(f) of the 1964 Salary Reform Act). Removal of a placement operates prospectively; pay already received is a completed historical consequence, and no entitlement, transfer of functions or right is preserved. Neither the acting order nor EO 11708 contains a savings or incumbent-protection clause for this order's items. The only carve-out, EO 11708 sec. 3's exception for the positions listed in its sec. 2, does not cover them; EO 11768's incumbent clause (1974) concerns its own list.

savings_residuals.reason: The order only placed, removed or renumbered positions in pay levels IV and V of the Executive Schedule under 5 U.S.C. 5317 (formerly sec. 303(f) of the 1964 Salary Reform Act). Removal of a placement operates prospectively; pay already received is a completed historical consequence, and no entitlement, transfer of functions or right is preserved. Neither the acting order nor EO 11708 contains a savings or incumbent-protection clause for this order's items. The only carve-out, EO 11708 sec. 3's exception for the positions listed in its sec. 2, does not cover them; EO 11768's incumbent clause (1974) concerns its own list.

unresolved_material_gaps: Clause EO:11262#sec1-item4-level-IV: the actual termination date of the President's Commission on Law Enforcement and Administration of Justice is not in held sources (EO 11236: terminate not later than 90 days after the final report). The clause ended on that date or, at the latest, on 1968-04-29 (EO 11409 item 1(b)). Needs the commission's report and termination record.
claim.research_rationale: EO 11262 adds three items to EO 11248: in level IV, (4) Executive Secretary of the President's Commission on Law Enforcement and Administration of Justice; in level V, (4) Director, Bureau of Outdoor Recreation and (5) Assistant to the Secretary of Defense (Legislative Affairs). No later amender deleted the two level V items (traced item by item through EO 11699); they ended with EO 11708 sec. 3 on March 23, 1973. EO 11409 item 1(b) formally deleted the level IV item on April 29, 1968. That position, however, belonged to a temporary commission: EO 11236 (held, 30 FR 9349) required the commission to report within 18 months and to terminate not later than 90 days after its report. The placement therefore probably lost its object before the 1968 deletion. Deadlines cannot fix the actual date, so that clause's first_end stays open. The whole-order end is unaffected because the two level V items ran to 1973-03-23. Family method: the researcher read the saved official Federal Register OCR text layers (heading to FR Doc line) of this order, of EO 11248 and of all 40 orders that the OFR disposition notes and the 1989 Codification list as amending it, plus EO 11708, 11715, 11736 and 11768, and traced every item of EO 11248 sections 1 and 2 through each addition, deletion, word substitution and renumbering. EO 11708 sec. 3 (signed and filed March 23, 1973; no other effective date) revokes EO 11248 as amended, except for the eight positions listed in its section 2; none of them is a position whose placement this order's text still supplied. Where a later amender deletes an item and inserts another in its place, the earlier item's placement ends on that amender's effective date; the series' separate 'substituting for the words' formula is treated as a retitling that continues the item. Pure deletions, renumberings and effective-date provisions are one-time edits completed when the order took effect. The 5 U.S.C. 5315-5316 amendment notes for 1964-1973 record no statutory placement of the positions concerned. Abolition of a position by unpublished departmental action is outside the held sources and is a limitation of this bounded search. Page images were not viewed; quotations are exact from the saved OCR, including its recognition errors. No human certification is asserted.
